_purpose: The pinned OUTSIDE composition source for the foods recommender. USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy release 2018-04 -- a US Government work in the public domain. It supplies COMPOSITION ONLY: how much of a nutrient is in a food, and how much a household portion weighs. It supplies NO target, dose, range, daily amount, deficiency sign or health claim -- every denominator in this app remains Dr. Wallach's. Ruled admissible by Luneth on 2026-08-21; see chronicle/contradictions/2026-08-21-usda-food-composition-third-source.md for the full reasoning, including that Wallach himself quantifies foods in USDA units (Hell's Kitchen: cashews, pistachios, hazelnuts) and cites USDA food tables by name (Immortality), and that this project already ships the USDA's 277-food ORAC list on his citation.
_archive_is_gitignored: The 6 MB archive itself is NOT committed (see .gitignore). It is re-downloadable in one command from `url` and verified against `sha256`. The rows this app actually uses are committed byte-exact in usda-extract.csv, so the composition gate runs on a fresh clone with no download.
publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service
licence: Public domain (17 U.S.C. 105 -- work of the U.S. Government). No attribution required; attributed anyway.

food_nutrient.csv.role: (fdc_id, nutrient_id) -> amount per 100 g. THE composition numbers.

food_portion.csv.role: portion id -> gram_weight for a household measure. THE serving sizes.

measure_unit.csv.role: measure_unit_id -> name, for rendering a portion label

nutrient_map._purpose: The ONLY place a Wallach essential slug is bound to a USDA nutrient id. One home (Charter R3). `usda_unit` is copied from nutrient.csv and the gate re-reads it -- it is never assumed. An essential absent from this map has NO USDA composition and is therefore unreachable by any food, which is stated honestly rather than filled in.

vitamin-a.note: Retinol Activity Equivalents, the form Wallach's mcg target is stated in.

no_usda_composition._purpose: Essentials that carry a numeric Wallach target but which SR Legacy does not measure. They are listed so the gap is explicit and auditable rather than silently absent. ★ THIS IS A GAP IN *THIS* SOURCE, NOT A VERDICT ON THE FOOD WORLD. On 2026-08-21 Luneth ruled that other reputable published sources may be pinned to reach them; iodine, flavonoids and silica are reached that way today, bound in eden/foods/sources/sources.json's `nutrient_bindings`, which is authoritative for any slug it names. The rest of this list still has no food source anywhere we hold and is still stated as a gap. NEVER fill one from a source that is not pinned, sha256-checked and re-extractable by the gate.

_display_why: The words the CARD uses for this source in the provenance gloss that sits on the number. Kept here, not in a view: a source name hand-typed into TypeScript is a second home for a fact (R3), and it is how a card keeps saying 'USDA' about a number that stopped coming from USDA.

support_nutrients._purpose: USDA nutrients the EXTRACT must carry that are NOT credited to any essential. They are not in nutrient_map because nothing on screen is measured against them; they are inputs to arithmetic. Keeping them in a separate list is what stops one from ever being mistaken for a Wallach-targeted essential (section 00.A).

water.why: Doleman 2017 publishes sulphur in umoles per gram of FREEZE-DRIED sample and never prints a moisture percentage, so the fresh-weight number a person needs has to be derived: dry_matter_fraction = 1 - water/100. This is that water.

linoleic.why: PUFA 18:2 — linoleic acid, one of Wallach's two essential fatty acids ('only two (linoleic and linolenic) are designated as Essential Fatty Acids'). The AGGREGATE 18:2 is used, not the specific 1316 (18:2 n-6 c,c): aggregate covers 186 of 190 catalog foods where the specific form covers 26.

linolenic.why: PUFA 18:3 — linolenic acid, the other EFA. Aggregate for the same reason as 18:2: 1404 (the specific ALA) covers only 33 of 190 foods.

conjugated_linoleic.why: PUFA 18:2 CLAs — SUBTRACTED from the 18:2 aggregate, because the aggregate includes it and conjugated linoleic acid is not the essential fatty acid Wallach names. 0-0.7% of 18:2 in the nuts and seeds that qualify.

epa.why: PUFA 20:5 n-3 — eicosapentaenoic acid, one of the two MARINE forms Wallach files under omega-3: 'further divided into the Omega-3 (DHA and EPA)' (Epigenetics, 2014). He names salmon oil as an essential-fatty-acid source interchangeable with flaxseed oil at the SAME dose — 'taken alternately as salmon oil and flaxseed oil at the rate of 5 grams t.i.d.' (Let's Play Doctor, 1995) — and calls cold-water fish 'rich sources of the essential fatty acids' (Rare Earths, 1994). Added 2026-08-31. Until then this row was never extracted, so a food's EFA was its 18:2/18:3 alone: canned salmon scored 1.5% of his nine grams and fell off the omega-3 list while pork ribs sat at 36%, and a fish-oil softgel was credited its full label oil mass. Owner ruling, Luneth 2026-08-31.

dha.why: PUFA 22:6 n-3 — docosahexaenoic acid, the other marine form named in that same sentence. Converted against SALMON oil, never flaxseed oil: in this same pinned archive flaxseed oil (fdc 167702) reads 0.000 g of BOTH 20:5 and 22:6, so flax-equivalent grams are not a currency a fish can be paid in. See _efa_why_two_oils in this file.

support_nutrients._efa_why_no_dpa: USDA 1280 (22:5 n-3, docosapentaenoic acid) is an omega-3 and is deliberately NOT extracted. Wallach names EPA and DHA; he never names DPA. Adding a form he does not name to a meter measured against his nine grams would be widening his claim by inference, which is the silent guess section 00.A forbids — so the marine numerator and the salmon-oil denominator both stop where his words stop. Salmon oil carries 2.991 g of it per 100 g, so including it would move a fish by roughly a tenth; the reason to leave it out is the rule, not the size.
support_nutrients._efa_why_two_oils: The EFA meter converts a food's ACID into the OIL Wallach doses, and he doses TWO. The 18:2/18:3 share converts against flaxseed oil (fdc 167702, 67.695% LA+ALA); the 20:5/22:6 share converts against salmon oil (fdc 172343, 31.255% EPA+DHA). Both fractions are read from the pinned archive at derive time, never typed. One oil for both shares was tried first and is wrong in the direction that matters: flaxseed oil contains none of what a fish carries.
support_nutrients._efa_why_here: These five are NOT in nutrient_map and must never be: omega-3 and omega-6 carry no individual Wallach target — he states ONE amount for the essential fatty acids as a category — so a food credited against either would be measured against a number that does not exist. They are inputs to the EFA aggregate instead, which is the same shape the 34 plant-derived minerals already use.
